correctness.rationale: Reconstructed exactly the source analytic-symbol Theorems 1.4 and 1.6 hypotheses on upper half-plane alpha>-1, power weights mu=y^u,lambda=y^v with |u|,|v|<alpha+1, Bloom weight nu=y^s where s=(u-v)/2 and |s|<alpha+1. For pole strictly below boundary b(z)=(z-zeta)^(-r), r>0, translate and dilate to (z+i)^(-r). The BMO oscillation denominator is proportional to L^(alpha+s+2). On boxes L<=R/4, derivative yields O(L^(1-s) R^(-r-1)); L>R/4, direct decay integration gives O(L^(-r-s)), with integrable-tail cases handled when r>=alpha+2. Small boxes with I=[0,L] have positive asymptotic c L^(1-s); boxes I=[L,2L] at infinity c L^(-r-s). Both directions give BMOA iff -r<=s<=1. Uniform vanishing in the two box regimes (small L and escaping center) holds iff strict -r<s<1, with the same witnesses giving nonvanishing at both endpoints. Theorem 1.4/1.6 convert these precisely into boundedness/compactness of both [b,P_alpha] and [b,P_alpha^+]. No false conclusion from discrete samples.
